## Highlights

- A chat filed in a project can now answer as one of the project's own agents: with the agent's instructions and equipped skills, and with its model when you may use that model in chat; otherwise your model answers, and the menu says so. The message box now shows the chat's project, and in a project with agents of its own, a second button beside it names who answers: one of the project's agents, or **Assistant**, the workspace's chat assistant. A new chat starts with the project's **Default chat agent**, which is **First agent created**, the oldest agent the project still has, unless anyone who can edit the project (Owners, Admins, Developers and Editors) chose another agent or **Assistant** under **Chats** on the project's **General** page. Only the chat's owner can switch who answers. In a chat you continue, choosing another project in the message box moves the chat, as **Move to project…** does, and from its next reply it answers as the new project's default; a chat taken out of its project answers as the assistant. Moving a chat that is shared with its project ends that share, so Tale asks first. When an agent is deleted, the chats that answered as it answer as the assistant, and a project whose default it was starts its new chats with the first agent created. The agent's name and an **Agent** mark stand above each reply it wrote, and **Create task** in such a chat fills in the chat's agent as the **Assignee**. The agent's runtime, connectors, platform tools and secrets stay with its tasks. Over the REST API, a message sent to a chat whose owner chose an agent is answered by that agent, and the message reads don't name it; a chat the API creates answers as the assistant, and the API can't choose an agent ([#5361](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5361), [#5362](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5362), [#5364](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5364)). See [Choose who answers in a project chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#who-answers) and [Respect thread scope and access](https://docs.tale.dev/develop/api-reference#respect-thread-scope-and-access).
- You can ask a chat to create a project, to change a project's name, description, instructions or default chat agent, to add an agent to a project, or to change an agent's name, instructions, model or skills. The chat changes nothing itself: it reads the projects you can open and shows the change as a card under its reply, with each field a new project or agent gets, or what a field is now and what it becomes. Nothing changes until you, the chat's owner, select **Apply**, which makes exactly that change, once, as you and with the same checks as the project's pages; the audit log's entries for it say that it came from the chat, and name the conversation and the proposal. **Dismiss** leaves everything as it was. The card then reads **Applied** or **Dismissed** and keeps that outcome when you come back. If what the card changes was changed since, for example by a colleague who edited the agent, **Apply** changes nothing, and the card reads **Not applied** with the reason. Editors, Developers, Admins and Owners chatting in the app get these proposals, with no setting to turn on; a Member's chat can describe a change but not propose it, and a message sent through the API gets none. In a chat filed in a project, the chat reads and changes that project only, though it can still propose a new project. A project created from a card is open to everyone in the organization; an Owner or Admin can limit it to teams under **Audience** in the **Sharing** section of its **General** page. Sharing, secrets, connectors, an agent's tools, repository access and deleting a project or an agent stay on the project's pages ([#5363](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5363)). See [Create or change projects and agents from chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#proposals).
- When the assistant reads a web page in a chat, it now reads the page's main content, without the site's navigation, the page's header and footer, dialogs or a cookie notice, and learns the page's canonical address when it read the page at another one ([#5036](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5036)). A page whose scripts build its content in the browser, or whose site first runs a check that a browser passes on its own, such as a challenge of Cloudflare, AWS WAF, Vercel or Fastly, is now opened once in a sandboxed browser, and its step reads **Reading example.com in a browser** ([#5183](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5183)). That browser introduces itself as `TaleAssistant`, never solves a CAPTCHA, and takes one of the organization's **Render sessions**, which website crawling uses too; a reply opens a page in it at most once. A CAPTCHA or a refusal that the site answers is never opened in the browser, and is no longer asked again through the deployment's other outbound proxies. A step that read nothing now says why in your language, on its line and when you expand it, for example **The site asks for a CAPTCHA**, **The site keeps automated readers out**, **No browser is free right now** or **The site didn't answer in time**; before, it read **Failed**, and its detail showed an English instruction meant for the model. The model no longer gets the words a site chose for an error status, or the deployment's setup errors when a render can't run, and a page's title reaches it cleaned and cut to 200 characters. See [Check what the assistant used](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#check-what-the-assistant-used).
- A message with documents attached no longer waits for their search index. Right after an upload, a worker reads each document's text with the indexer's own extraction and puts it through the organization's secret scan and **PII protection**, as indexing does, and the message waits only for those reads, which take seconds. Before, it waited until each document was indexed, behind every other upload, and two documents in one message could leave it queued for good, its chips at **Indexing…**. Only a document too large to read before its index still holds the message until its indexing finishes: a PDF, Word, PowerPoint or OpenDocument file over 50 MiB, a spreadsheet over 20 MiB, a text file over 4 MiB, or a file with more than about four million characters of text. A document's chip reads **Reading…**, then its size, or why the assistant can't read it, such as **Can't be read**, **No readable text** or **Can't be opened**, in your language; the reason also opens on keyboard focus. A file the organization's checks refused, or are still checking, is kept out of the code the assistant runs, a task agent's workspace and an agent review, and a task's brief names it. The assistant also knows each attachment's type and size. The search index now takes one file per slot, for every upload: one slow file no longer holds the files fetched with it for up to 15 minutes and then fails them all. A queued message whose reply comes quickly now shows that reply without a reload; before, it looked as though the message had never been sent. See [Send while processing continues](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/attachments#send-while-processing-continues).
- IBANs are now masked, blocked or tokenized as an organization's **PII protection** says. Since v0.5.0, the backend's runtime recognized no IBAN, so none was protected: not in chat messages, not in requests to the model endpoints, and not in documents and attachments being indexed or read for the assistant. See [Protect personal data](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/guardrails#protect-personal-data).
- The sandboxed browser that renders pages, for website crawling and now for chats, sends every request through the sandbox's egress proxy. Before, a rendered page's scripts could reach the services beside the sandbox directly, past the proxy that refuses such addresses. A crawl now also reads a page behind a bot check the browser passes, such as Cloudflare's or AWS WAF's: the browser waits for the reload the check makes, and the page's status is that of the document it ends on. Before, the crawl took the check for the page and charged the page a failure, such as `HTTP 403 at render time`.
- After a sign-in through your organization's SSO, through its authenticating proxy, or with a passkey you added during such a sign-in, you can now create your own API key under **Settings > API > REST** when your role (Owner, Admin or Developer) or a competence an Admin granted allows keys. Before, such a session refused it with `403 ORG_FORBIDDEN`, whatever the role. The key works in that organization only, and **Belongs to** reads **You — this organization only**: it acts as you with your current role there, needs no `X-Organization-Slug`, ends when you leave the organization and shares your rate-limit allowance. The organization's Owners and Admins see it and can revoke it, except that an Admin can't revoke an Owner's. Such a session no longer offers **Revoke key** on your older keys that work in every organization, which it can't revoke: the page says to revoke them after a password sign-in. Owners and Admins can also choose **All keys in this organization** beside **Keys you manage**, which adds the keys members made for themselves after a password sign-in: read-only, with the holder's name and email, and with **Last used** reading **Not available**, since such a key also works in the holder's other organizations. The create dialog now says why its **Member** list leaves someone out and when a key won't reach the model endpoints, and a refusal to create a key reads in your language. See [Your key after an SSO sign-in](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/api-keys#your-key-after-sso).
- A project's **Agents** tab now says who can use its agents, under **Who can use these agents**: **Org-wide**, or the teams the project is limited to. An agent is shared with everyone who can open its project, so to share one with the whole organization, create it in a project open to everyone. The docs now say how, and that only Owners and Admins change who can open a project once it exists; the pages that said only the assistant answers in a project chat, or that Editors change a project's audience, are corrected. See [Share an agent with everyone](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/project-agents#share-an-agent).
- A deck the built-in `pptx` skill builds from a template now keeps the template's sections in step with its slides. Before, the deleted template slides stayed listed in their sections and the new slides sat in none, so PowerPoint showed every template section as empty, "(0)", beside the new slides. Now a deleted slide leaves its section, a new slide joins the section of the slide before it, a copied slide joins its source's section, and the sections left empty go; a template's instruction and toolbox slides are deleted unless you ask to keep them, and the skill checks each section's slides before it finishes. An edit of your own deck keeps its empty sections. A deck the skill's scripts can't read, such as a damaged or encrypted file, stops them with one error line before they change anything. An organization created before this release keeps the skill it was created with: see the upgrade notes ([#4964](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4964)).
- A follow-up question in a chat whose earlier replies read web pages, files or search results no longer sends those results to the model cut to 400 characters while the conversation still fits the model's context window. Beside such a stub, the earlier answer read as one the model could not have known, so a model such as Claude Sonnet 5.5 began its next reply by correcting a truthful answer and read the pages again. The whole history now goes to the model while it fits. When it no longer fits, Tale first shortens the oldest results, each with a note that it was read whole when the answer after it was written, and leaves out the oldest messages only when that is not enough. Text that you or the assistant wrote is never shortened, and the assistant is told what was shortened or left out ([#5356](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5356)). See [Continue, copy, or keep the conversation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#continue-copy-or-keep-the-conversation).
- A file the assistant makes now shows once, under its reply. When the model also wrote the file's reference into its text, as a picture or a link, the picture showed a second time as a grey placeholder whose preview opened empty. Now a picture of a file the reply made is not repeated in the text, a link to a stored file opens its preview, a stored picture in the text is shown only when you may open it, and a picture that can't be shown reads as its description. Copying a reply leaves the references out ([#5358](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5358)). See [Open and download the files](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/files-and-skills#open-and-download-the-files).
- Pictures in a chat that stays open for more than 15 minutes no longer break. A picture's link lives 15 minutes, and the page kept the links for as long as it stayed open, so opening a picture after that showed a broken image in **Image preview**. A picture or preview whose link has run out now gets a new link and draws from it, and shows the file's card when that fails too. This covers the pictures under a reply, a stored picture a reply's text names, the photos attached to a message and the previews of a task's pictures ([#5366](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5366)).
- A colleague reading a chat shared with its project no longer fills the browser's console with errors: the page asked for the reply's live stream and the chat's video links, which only the chat's owner may read, and got 404 each time, for the video links again and again. A reader now sees the conversation without an answer still being written, and the finished answer when they reload the chat ([#5383](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5383)). See [Keep personal and shared chats distinct](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/concepts#keep-personal-and-shared-chats-distinct).
- Screen readers now read a project's name once where the project's icon stands beside it: in the project and chat rows of **Home**, in a chat's header and in the **Projects** list. The icon was an image named after the project, so the name was read twice ([#5382](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5382)).
- Code in CSV, and in every other language outside the 39 whose highlighting loads first, is now highlighted in the browser, in a file's preview and in the code blocks of a reply. It showed as plain text, with a warning in the browser's console ([#5384](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5384)).
- On a slow Docker host, a sandbox session, such as the worker a project agent's task runs in, no longer fails to start after 30 seconds while most of its start-up time is left. Its container now has whatever remains of the whole start-up budget, `SANDBOX_SESSION_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 seconds by default). A start that runs out of that time now says that it timed out, how long it had and which variable sets the budget, and keeps what Docker printed, where its error read `docker run (session) failed:` with nothing after it ([#5280](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5280)).
- **Session Manager** now shows its frame as soon as a page arrives: its side rail, or its tab bar on a phone, with placeholders where the icons go. Before, every page stayed blank until its scripts had loaded. An empty **Sessions**, **Proxies** or **Secrets** page now opens on its empty state, such as **No proxies yet**, where it first showed a toolbar and placeholder rows and then flickered to the empty state; a list with rows shows as many placeholder rows as it has rows, up to twelve, while they load.
- In a **Session Manager** session whose proxy needs a user name and password, an answer that the browser reads more slowly than the proxy sends it no longer loses its end after the browser has closed its side of the connection: it arrives whole ([#5387](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5387)).

## Upgrade notes

- At start, the backend applies `0236_chat_agents.sql`, `0237_chat_proposals.sql` and `0238_file_metadata_text_reads.sql`. The first adds who answers to each conversation and each project's default chat agent; the second adds the table that keeps the changes chats propose, with their outcome; the third adds three nullable columns to each file's row that say where its read for the assistant stands, a check on them that is added `NOT VALID`, so no existing row is scanned, and an index of the reads still pending. They add only nullable or defaulted columns, indexes, a check and a new table, which the previous image never reads, so they are safe during a rolling deploy, and no operator step is needed.
- The knowledge database gets `services/db/migrations/knowledge-db/private_knowledge/00000000000020_document_reads.sql`: a new, empty table, `private_knowledge.document_reads`, that keeps a document's checked text until its index holds it. It creates the table only if it is missing and changes no existing row. It runs at start: the `knowledge-db` service applies it with dbmate before it reports ready, and the backend's worker applies it when it starts too, which covers a database container the upgrade leaves running, such as the `db` service that `tale deploy` keeps up. An organization that keeps its knowledge in a database of its own gets the table when Tale first uses that database. It is safe during a rolling deploy, since the previous image never reads the table, and no operator step is needed. The API contract stays at `3.52.0`.
- After the upgrade, the new chats of a project with agents of its own answer as its first agent created, and chats that already exist keep the assistant. To keep the assistant for a project's new chats, anyone who can edit the project (Owners, Admins, Developers and Editors) chooses **Assistant** under **Default chat agent** on the project's **General** page.
- Where **PII protection** covers IBANs, the chat messages sent before the upgrade reached the model with their IBANs, and the documents and attachments indexed before it keep their IBANs in the index until they are indexed again. For a document under **Knowledge**, **Reindex** in its row menu does that.
- Reading a page in a browser from a chat needs no new service, variable or image: it uses what website crawling uses, the `sandbox` service with its `SANDBOX_TOKEN`, and one of the organization's **Render sessions** under **Settings > Sandboxes** (2 by default, shared with crawling). An Owner or Admin can raise that limit when chats often read **No browser is free right now**. The browser goes out through `sandbox-egress` and the outbound proxies of `OUTBOUND_PROXY_URLS`, as a crawl does. On a deployment without the sandbox service, such a page's step reads **The page couldn't be opened in a browser**, and every other page reads as before.
- Integrations need no change: a chat the REST API creates answers as the assistant, and the API can't choose an agent. A message an integration sends to a project chat whose owner chose an agent in the app is answered by that agent. Every existing API key reaches what it reached before; a key someone makes for themselves after an SSO sign-in works in that organization only and needs no `X-Organization-Slug`.
- The pptx fixes are in the built-in `pptx` skill, which an organization receives only when it is created, so an existing organization keeps the skill it has. To take the new one, an Owner or Admin uploads the folder `configs/platform/custom/skills/pptx` of the v0.5.101 source under **Settings > Skills** with **Add skill > Upload folder** and confirms **Replace**; **Created by** then names them instead of **Built-in**. `tale deploy --override-all` replaces it too, but also resets the rest of every organization's configuration, governance and PII policies included, to the shipped defaults.
- `tale deploy` neither pulls nor starts the Session Manager. Its fixes take effect when you pull its released image again, for example with `PULL_POLICY=always docker compose -f compose.session-manager.yml up -d`; its configuration needs no change.
- No configuration, limit, credential or sign-in setting needs to change beyond these: the other fixes take effect with the new images.
